title: Steve Eisman's Masterclass on the 2008 Financial Crisis (Part Two) | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 39
summary: Eisman traces crisis contagion through retained mortgage exposures and CDS, criticizes underwriting due diligence, and argues that post-crisis capital and liquidity rules made large banks safer. He explains SVB as concentrated uninsured funding combined with duration risk, then favors targeted regulatory easing and consolidation. Primary records support the core SVB mechanism and substantial post-crisis recapitalization. Important qualifications concern HTM accounting, blanket bailout protection, nonrandom due-diligence samples and claims that SVB posed no systemic danger. The concluding multi-year bank outlook remains conditional and only partly observable.
assessment: Full transcript read. This bounded evidence audit retains unresolved outcomes where matched primary verification is missing; those are not adverse accuracy grades.
speaker_map_notes: Steve Eisman is the sole substantive speaker; viewer questions are distinguished from his responses.
framework_points: Examine where distributed credit risk ultimately remains.
A hedge adds counterparty dependence rather than eliminating all risk.
Distinguish asset credit risk, duration risk and liability concentration.
Assess regulation through behavior and unintended consequences, not only stated intentions.
Separate earnings pressure from immediate liquidity failure, while recognizing economic capital losses.
tools_and_charts: Illustrative GE bond plus CDS premium
Clayton loan-file samples and defect rates
2009 bank stress tests and capital raises
SVB asset duration, uninsured deposits, unrealized losses and VC cash burn
Bank deposit-share and compliance/technology scale comparisons
transcript_cautions: Opening montage repeats the substantive discussion.
December upload contains references framed around June 27, 2025; recording date is not established, so policy announcements before publication are not automatically credited as forecasts.
Names including Tarullo, Paulson and Geithner are garbled in captions but identifiable.
He explicitly labels the theory that Geithner stopped prosecutions as unproven; it is not extracted as his factual assertion.

claims.claim: Regulation should become somewhat more lenient under Bowman, including stress testing and compliance, without returning to the pre-Dodd-Frank regime.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Establish recording date, then compare rules announced afterward and realized compliance burden.
claims.reason: Targeted leverage easing became effective in 2026 and stress-capital requirements were held until 2027. However the eSLR rule was finalized before the December upload, and uncertain recording date prevents treating all of this as out-of-sample foresight; specific compliance savings remain unverified.

evidence.title: Agencies issue final rule modifying regulatory capital standards
evidence.finding: Final eSLR changes effective April 1, 2026, with January opt-in. Agencies estimate under 2% reduction in holding-company Tier 1 requirements, larger subsidiary reductions constrained by holding-company capital rules. Demonstrates targeted easing, not return to pre-crisis regulation.

evidence.title: 2026 annual bank stress-test results
evidence.finding: All 32 banks remained above CET1 minimums in the specified hypothetical recession; $708 billion projected losses, 1.6-point aggregate capital decline. Capital requirements stay in place until 2027. Model results are not guarantees against every shock.

claims.next_check: Obtain primary evidence matching the stated metric, period and conditions before assigning an outcome grade.

claims.claim: June 2025 stress-test results already demonstrate a more favorable regulatory environment for banks.
claims.speaker: Steve Eisman
claims.test: Reconcile changes in losses and capital requirements with scenario design and portfolio composition.
claims.reason: The results show buffers under defined assumptions; they do not alone establish that a political change caused easier outcomes. Scenario, portfolio and model changes must be separated.

evidence.title: 2025 stress-test results, revised September 30
evidence.finding: Aggregate CET1 13.4% at start, hypothetical trough 11.6%; institution-specific outcomes and separate leverage ratios are disclosed. Results reflect scenario, portfolio and model assumptions, not a direct measure of political intent.

claims.next_check: Obtain primary evidence matching the stated metric, period and conditions before assigning an outcome grade.
